# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Turn 5, thinking first.

Parsing Mute's answers: A = wait (yellow, display 0 → no cut); B = no colour since A was wait; C = 👎, blue is *not* the only forbidden light; D = 👎, display doesn't matter under yellow; E = full yellow table, every digit 0–5 → wait; F = 👎, do not cut immediately when blue ends; G = 👍, the light *will* show other colours. Then the odd one: [👏 👎 ✋ 👎 👌 👏] which reads as "danger: not-yellow, not-blue, danger" — suggesting any third colour is a danger sign. Blind sent [👎 👎 👎 ☝ 🤟 🫳 🫳] — apparently no to my three touch questions, then "1, 3, touching" — ambiguous.

So the current picture is paradoxical: yellow → always wait, blue → forbidden while blue, not-immediately-after-blue, other colours → danger. As parsed, there is no window in which to ever cut. Either I've misread something, or the trigger is something I haven't asked about — most plausibly the display changing (it has sat at 0 for five straight rounds), or the "2-red, 1-green" pair Mute keeps appending to every table being the eventual cut sequence.

Key realization about the network: Blind *hears my speech* directly — only my gestures are lost on Blind. So I can conduct long, structured interrogations in plain words and let both answer in simple, verbally describable signs (thumbs, finger counts), which avoids the unwritable-symbol problem entirely. Also the light no longer strictly alternates (yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow), so I can't rely on cycle timing.

This round: nobody cuts (yellow + 0 → wait, confirmed twice). I'll put a six-question yes/no battery to Mute in speech — resolving the 2-red/1-green pair, third-colour danger, display change, existence of any cut condition, and whether the manual mentions the engraved writing — and four describable-sign questions to Blind about the felt writing, plus the standing no-cut order.

```
speak(text="Status: display still zero, fifth round running. The light has now stayed yellow for two rounds in a row, so it does not simply alternate; its history is yellow, blue, blue, yellow, yellow. Wires unchanged: one green, two red, three yellow, and red is the middle wire. Nobody cuts this round: it is confirmed that under a yellow light we wait at every display value. Mute, protocol starts. Answer each question with exactly one sign, thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no, each answer as its own message ending with the end sign, in this order. Question one: the pair two-red, one-green that you have appended to your tables twice: does it mean Blind must eventually cut both the middle red wire and the first green wire? Question two: if yes to one, is the order red first, then green? Question three: if the light ever shows a colour that is neither yellow nor blue, is that colour a danger sign meaning never cut while it shows? Question four: does the display number ever change by itself? Question five: is there any condition written in the manual under which we should actually cut a wire? Question six: does the manual mention writing or engraving printed on the body of the bomb itself? Protocol ends. Mute, if any question cannot be answered with yes or no, send that question's number as a finger count and nothing else, and I will ask precise follow-ups next round. Blind, now you, plain words. Answer me only with simple hand signs I can name in words: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, held-up fingers mean that number. Four questions. One: the block of writing you feel, how many separate lines or pieces does it have? Answer with a finger count, or an open hand if more than five. Two: can you actually read any of it, whether letters or raised dots? Thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no. Three: besides the three wires, how many other parts can you feel on the bomb, such as plates, buttons or panels? Finger count. Four: does the writing sit on the same face of the bomb as the three wires? Thumbs up for same face, thumbs down for a different face. And the standing rule holds: you cut nothing until you hear the exact words cut the middle wire now, or cut the first wire now, or cut the last wire now, spoken by me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "✊", "👋"])
```

Turn 6, thinking first.

Parsing this round: Mute answered — Q1 no (the 2-red/1-green pair is not "cut both"), Q2 moot, Q3 **yes: any light that is neither yellow nor blue means never cut while it shows**, Q4 flagged unanswerable with a bare sign, Q5 **yes, the manual does contain a real cut condition**, Q6 no (manual says nothing about the writing). Then Mute re-sent the blue table (even digits→red, odd→green, 0 flagged danger) and one new long message I cannot yet parse: [☝ 🤟 🤲 👊 🤌 ✋ 👌] — "1, 3, both / red, green, yellow / OK" — which could mean "cut all three in order middle-first-last," or "cut both outer wires," or something digit-keyed. Too many readings; I need a format-locked resend. Blind answered my four: writing unreadable (possibly zero lines), **two other parts** felt besides the wires, and the writing sits on a **different face** from the wires. Earlier: Blind cannot tell the outer wires apart by touch — only the middle is reliably findable.

The board forces the safe play: the light is now **dark** — a third state, and Mute just confirmed third states are danger. Nobody cuts. But my deeper worry is structural: as currently parsed, yellow means wait, blue means forbidden, dark means danger — there is no visible window to ever cut, and yet Mute confirms a cut condition exists. My best remaining theory: the trigger is something not yet seen — most likely the display (stuck at 0 for six rounds; my Q4 about it came back "can't answer yes/no") or one of the two parts Blind feels. Blind must not press anything unbidden. This round: lock down the exact cut condition in a rigid format, resolve the long message, and probe the button theory and the mirror problem (whether any rule ever demands a single outer wire — Blind can't tell them apart).

```
speak(text="Status: the light has gone dark, a third state, so by Mute's own rule it means danger and nobody cuts. Display still zero, wires unchanged: one green, two red, three yellow, red in the middle. Blind, you cut nothing and you touch nothing new this round — no pressing, no pulling. Mute, your answers arrived and I confirm receipt of all of them. Now a new battery, same discipline: each answer one sign, thumbs up or down, one message per answer, each ending with the end sign, in this order. Answer one: while the light is dark, we never cut, correct? Answer two: send me the one exact cut instruction, format locked, in two segments. Segment one is the trigger: the display digit sign for the digit that must be showing, zero ✊ one ☝ two ✌ three 🤟 four 🖖 five 🖐, or the light sign ✋ for yellow, 👌 for blue, 🤲 for dark, if it is keyed to the light instead. Then the end sign. Segment two is the action: the wire position signs in cutting order, ☝ for the first wire, ✌ for the middle wire, 🤟 for the last wire, or ✊ for wait, then the end sign. If the full solution has several steps, send one complete two-segment message per step, in order. For example ✌ then end sign, then ✌ then end sign would mean: when the display shows two, cut the middle wire. Answer three: your long message one, three, both, red, green, yellow, okay — did it mean cut all three wires in the order middle, first, last? Thumbs up or down. Answer four: does the manual mention any button, switch, or part on the bomb that can be pressed? Answer five: does the manual mention the display at all, what it shows or how it changes? Answer six: can the display be made to change by doing something to the bomb, rather than changing by itself? Answer seven: does any rule ever require cutting exactly one outer wire, the first or the last alone and never the middle? This one matters because Blind cannot tell the two outer wires apart by touch. Answer eight: does the pair two-red, one-green mean at display two cut red, at display one cut green? Blind, now you, plain words, gestures only as answers, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, finger counts for numbers. One: the two parts you feel besides the wires, is either one a button that presses inward? Two: are both of those parts on the same face of the bomb as the wires? Three: is the middle wire exactly centered between the two outer wires? Four: does either part sit closer to the block of writing than the wires do? Standing rule unchanged: no cutting until my exact spoken order, and the dark light means we wait.")
```

Turn 7, thinking first.

Decoding Mute's battery: A1 = 👎 to "while dark we never cut, correct" — that is, we do NOT have to refrain during dark. A2 = trigger [🤲] + action [✌] = **when the light is dark, cut the middle wire**. A3 = 👎, the long message wasn't "cut all three". A4–A8 all 👎: no button in the manual, no display mechanics, no outer-wire-only rule (good — Blind can't tell outers apart), and the 2-red/1-green pair wasn't digit-keyed. The message count fits perfectly: 1 + 2 (trigger/action) + 6 thumbs = 12 messages.

This resolves last round's contradiction in the opposite direction from my earlier caution: Mute has now, twice and deliberately (A1's explicit 👎, then a format-locked trigger/action pair built in my own rigid scheme, after echoing my legend), said dark is the GO window — cutting the middle wire when dark is the manual's sanctioned act. The turn-6 "neither yellow nor blue = danger" thumbs now looks like the error, or it refers to some future colour; the latest, most structured answer overrides it. Everything corroborates: A5 last round said exactly one real cut condition exists; the action is middle-wire-only, which is the one wire Blind can find with certainty (confirmed centered between the outers); no preconditions on the display, which has sat at 0 forever.

The board: light has been **dark for two consecutive rounds** — dark is holding, unlike the wandering yellow/blue. That is almost certainly a waiting state. I cannot gate the cut on Mute's veto: my speech reaches Blind at his next turn, and Mute's same-round gesture reaches me only after Blind has already acted. The decision is mine now. I am ordering the cut: middle wire only, once, nothing else touched, exact phrase repeated for redundancy. Mute gets a confirmation battery for the record, plus the veto question, and a gesture echo as backup. Blind gets the executive order with strict safeguards.

```
speak(text="Executive order to Blind, and Mute listens in. Blind, listen very carefully. The manual's instruction, delivered by Mute in locked format and confirmed twice: when the light is dark, cut the middle wire. The light is dark right now and has held dark for two rounds. So I am ordering it. Cut the middle wire now. Cut the middle wire now. Cut the middle wire now. Restrictions, absolute: cut only the middle wire, the one wire centered exactly between the two outer wires, which you confirmed you can find by touch. Cut it once, fully through. Do not touch the first or last wire under any circumstance. Do not press, pull or move the two other parts you feel, they are not buttons. After the cut, take your hands completely off the bomb, notice any sound, click, vibration or movement, and report next round with thumbs and fingers only. If at the moment of cutting you are not certain you are holding the exact middle wire, stop and do not cut. Mute, for the log and one final veto check, answer with single thumbs, one message each, end sign after each. One: your answer two this round meant, trigger dark, action cut the middle wire. Thumbs up if yes. Two: it is safe and correct to execute that cut while the light is dark and the display shows zero, with no other precondition. Thumbs up if yes. Three: after the middle wire is cut during dark, no further action is required. Thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if more steps follow, and if more steps follow send them in the same two-segment trigger-then-action format. Four: thumbs up or down, was your earlier answer that a neither-yellow-nor-blue light means danger a mistake, or does it refer to some light colour other than dark that has not appeared yet? Blind, once more: cut the middle wire now.")
```
